72	## Processing Pipeline
73	
74	```
75	Input (URL/YouTube/File)
76	  |-> Content Extraction
77	  |     YouTube: lib/youtube.py transcript extraction
78	  |     Web: processing/web_content_processor.py scraping
79	  |     File: direct read (supports .md, .pdf, .txt — NOT .docx; use bulk ingestion for docx)
80	  |
81	  |-> Knowledge Base Storage (lib/knowledge_base_crud.py)
82	  |     Indexes content, assigns doc_id
83	  |
84	  |-> Upstash Search Sync (lib/sync_to_upstash_search_integrated.py)
85	  |     Syncs to frontend search index (if configured)
86	  |
87	  |-> Entity Extraction (lib/entity_extraction/)
88	  |     NER + Xata database matching (85-95% accuracy)
89	  |     Extracts: personnel, organizations, locations, events
90	  |
91	  |-> CocoIndex Knowledge Graph (lib/cocoindex_integration.py)
92	  |     Builds entity relationships (requires PostgreSQL + Neo4j)
93	  |
94	  |-> Mem0 Contextual Memory (lib/mem0_integration.py)
95	  |     Stores processing summaries, entity memories
96	  |
97	  |-> Upstash Queue (lib/upstash/queue.py)
98	       QStash async processing for downstream consumers
99	```
100	
101	Each stage is fault-tolerant -- failures log warnings but never block the pipeline.

284	## Playlist Ingestion (`scripts/playlist_ingestion.py`)
285	
286	Batch-ingest one or more YouTube podcast playlists end-to-end. Each episode flows through: enumeration → transcript fetch → parse/clean → **fidelity review** (quality gate) → full pipeline (KB storage, NER entity extraction, vectorization, CocoIndex knowledge graph, Mem0).
287	
288	```bash
289	# One or more playlist URLs (plain video URLs also accepted)
290	python scripts/playlist_ingestion.py "https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL..." [MORE_URLS...]
291	
292	# From a file (one URL per line, # comments allowed), with vector store upload
293	python scripts/playlist_ingestion.py --from-file playlists.txt --upload
294	
295	# Preview a new playlist's caption quality without ingesting
296	python scripts/playlist_ingestion.py <URL> --limit 5 --dry-run
297	
298	# Stricter gate + LLM coherence pass (FIDELITY_REVIEW_MODEL, default gpt-5.5)
299	python scripts/playlist_ingestion.py <URL> --min-fidelity 0.6 --llm-review
300	```
301	
302	Flags: `--upload` (OpenAI vector store), `--no-kb`, `--limit N` (per playlist), `--force` (reprocess done episodes), `--dry-run`, `--min-fidelity 0.45`, `--llm-review`, `--delay 2.0` (seconds between episodes), `--state-file PATH`.
303	
304	**Resume is automatic**: state is checkpointed to `data/playlist_ingestion/state.json` after every episode; re-runs skip `ingested`/`quarantined` episodes and retry `failed`/`no_transcript` ones.
305	
306	**Fidelity review** (`lib/transcript_fidelity.py`) scores each transcript 0–1 from coverage, speech density (wpm), caption gaps, artifact ratio, and repetition; verdicts: `pass` ≥ 0.7, `review` ≥ 0.45, `fail` < 0.45. Failing/below-threshold episodes are **quarantined** (transcript + fidelity JSON kept on disk, not ingested). Artifacts: cleaned transcripts in `data/playlist_ingestion/transcripts/`, per-episode fidelity reports and per-run markdown summaries in `data/playlist_ingestion/reports/`.
307	
308	See [Playlist ingestion details](references/playlist-ingestion.md) for stage internals, state schema, quarantine review workflow, and tuning.
309

# Artifact runtime capabilities

A published Artifact page can declare **runtime capabilities** — abilities the claude.ai viewer grants the page at open time — by passing `capabilities: {name: config}` to the Artifact tool. The control plane is the authority on valid names and config shapes. Declaration gestures: **omitting** `capabilities` on a redeploy carries the stored declaration forward unchanged (and preserves the artifact's stored contract pin); an **empty object** `{}` is the explicit clear-all; a **non-empty object** is a full-set declaration (anything stored but not restated is revoked). Moving a republished artifact's runtime version is a deliberate gesture — pass `contract: 'latest'` to upgrade, or a specific version to pin or roll back — never a side effect of editing.

**Available capabilities:** `downloads`, `mcp` — the complete set of capability names you may declare. Anything not listed is unavailable to this user.

Runtime contract 0.1.22


--- capability: downloads ---

The `downloads` capability lets a published page offer a generated file to the viewer: declare `capabilities: {downloads: true}`, then call `window.claude.downloads.save({filename, data})`. The viewer sees a confirmation and may decline — a save is never silent or guaranteed, so offer it on explicit viewer intent and handle rejection. Check `window.claude.downloads` exists before first use; the type definitions are authoritative for the call contract and error codes.


--- capability: mcp ---

`mcp` lets a published page call the viewer's claude.ai connectors via `window.claude.mcp`; calls run with the viewer's credentials, never exposing tokens. Declare `capabilities: {mcp: {servers: [{server, tools}]}}` — `server` is a connector's display name. Keep the manifest minimal: it is a viewer-consented grant, and a declaring page cannot be shared publicly. Two arms: a section DISPLAYING data registers `watchTool(server, tool, input, handler, opts?)` — replays cache, refreshes when stale, polls only via `refetchInterval`, returns a sync unsubscribe to store; an ACTION calls `callTool` once and reads `result.payload`. Tool failures REJECT (`tool_error`); watch failures arrive as handler error events. Read the type definitions first: branch UX per error code, retry only `retryable` errors, drop data on authz denials, drive freshness UI from `result.cache.storedAt`. They omit argument names and result encoding: observe a real request/response pair per tool, or say so at publish — never guess.


**Your connectors this session.** None are connected right now — they may still be connecting, or the user has none. Look for tools prefixed `mcp__claude_ai_*` in your tool list; each is named `mcp__claude_ai_<connector>__<tool>`. Only claude.ai connectors are valid — locally-configured MCP servers are not. The manifest's `tools` array takes the connector's upstream tool names (as returned by `listTools()` / `/v1/mcp_servers`), which can differ from the normalized `<toolName>` segment when an upstream name contains `.` or spaces. In hermetic/CI sessions where connectors aren't loaded but `$CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` is set, fetch the list via Bash: `curl -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' -H 'anthropic-beta: mcp-servers-2025-12-04' -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN" https://api.anthropic.com/v1/mcp_servers?limit=1000`; in that case use each entry's `display_name` as the `server` value (exact display names are always accepted alongside tool-prefix segments).

The type definitions cover only the call envelope — they do not tell you a connector tool's argument names or its result encoding. Never publish a page that calls a connector tool without having observed one real request/response pair for that tool in this session; if you cannot safely observe one (for example, the connector is unauthenticated here, or calling the tool would have side effects), say that explicitly to the user at publish time — in your reply, not as a note inside the published page — instead of shipping a guessed shape. ```text
1	# Playlist Ingestion Reference
2	
3	Deep-dive on the YouTube podcast playlist pipeline (`scripts/playlist_ingestion.py`).
4	
5	## Stage-by-Stage Flow
6	
7	```
8	playlist URL(s)
9	  |-> Episode Enumeration
10	  |     yt-dlp flat extraction (no downloads; returns id, title, duration per entry)
11	  |     pytube fallback if yt-dlp fails
12	  |     Plain video URLs are treated as single-episode playlists
13	  |
14	  |-> Transcript Fetch (per episode)
15	  |     lib/youtube_transcript_enhanced.get_metadata_and_transcript_api_first()
16	  |     Cookie-free youtube-transcript-api + oEmbed metadata
17	  |     Returns a `reason` code, mapped to a status:
18	  |       no captions / captions disabled -> `no_transcript`  (retried next run)
19	  |       private / deleted / age-gated   -> `unavailable`     (terminal)
20	  |       YouTube blocked this IP         -> `blocked`         (retried; see below)
21	  |
22	  |-> Parse + Clean
23	  |     lib/transcript_fidelity.clean_transcript()
24	  |     Strips [Music]/[Applause]/[inaudible] cues, dedupes stuck caption
25	  |     lines, normalizes whitespace
26	  |     Cleaned copy saved to data/playlist_ingestion/transcripts/<video_id>.txt
27	  |
28	  |-> Fidelity Review
29	  |     lib/transcript_fidelity.review_transcript() -> FidelityReport
30	  |     Heuristic subscores (weights):
31	  |       coverage   .30  captions cover the episode's yt-dlp duration
32	  |       density    .20  words-per-minute in the 90-220 speech band
33	  |       gaps       .15  largest silence between caption segments
34	  |       artifacts  .15  non-speech cue ratio in raw text
35	  |       repetition .20  duplicate 6-gram windows (stuck captions)
36	  |     Optional --llm-review: samples 3 chunks, asks FIDELITY_REVIEW_MODEL
37	  |     (default gpt-5.5) for a coherence rating that becomes 1/3 of the score
38	  |     Verdicts: pass >= 0.7 | review 0.45-0.7 | fail < 0.45
39	  |     Report saved to data/playlist_ingestion/reports/<video_id>.fidelity.json
40	  |
41	  |-> Quality Gate
42	  |     verdict `fail` OR score < --min-fidelity -> status `quarantined`
43	  |     (transcript + report kept on disk for human review; NOT ingested)
44	  |
45	  |-> Full Pipeline (main.process_url)
46	        KB storage -> Upstash sync -> NER entity extraction ->
47	        vectorization (--upload -> OpenAI vector store) ->
48	        CocoIndex knowledge graph -> Mem0 memory
49	```
50	
51	## Checkpointing & Resume
52	
53	State lives in `data/playlist_ingestion/state.json`, keyed by video ID:
54	
55	```json
56	{
57	  "videos": {
58	    "dQw4w9WgXcQ": {
59	      "title": "...", "url": "...", "playlist_id": "PL...",
60	      "status": "ingested", "fidelity": 0.87, "doc_id": "abc123",
61	      "updated": "2026-07-23T18:00:00+00:00"
62	    }
63	  }
64	}
65	```
66	
67	- State is written after **every** episode (atomic tmp-file swap), so a crash
68	  or Ctrl-C loses at most the in-flight episode.
69	- Re-running the same playlist skips episodes whose status is `ingested`,
70	  `quarantined`, or `unavailable` (terminal). `no_transcript`, `blocked`,
71	  `enrichment_failed`, and `failed` episodes are retried automatically. Use
72	  `--force` to reprocess everything.
73	- Statuses: `ingested`, `quarantined`, `unavailable`, `no_transcript`,
74	  `blocked`, `enrichment_failed`, `failed`, `dry_run`, `skipped` (counted per
75	  run, not stored).
76	
77	## IP Blocks
78	
79	YouTube rate-limits the caption endpoint per IP. A block is a property of the
80	**run**, not of a video, so after `YT_BLOCKED_ABORT_THRESHOLD` consecutive
81	`blocked` episodes (default 3) the run aborts with exit code 2 rather than
82	walking the rest of the playlist and recording every episode as a failure.
83	Blocked episodes are not terminal — fix egress and re-run.
84	
85	Remedies, in `.env` or the environment:
86	
87	```bash
88	YT_WEBSHARE_PROXY_USERNAME=...   # Webshare rotating residential (preferred)
89	YT_WEBSHARE_PROXY_PASSWORD=...
90	YT_PROXY_URL=http://user:pass@host:port   # or any single HTTP(S) proxy
91	YT_TRANSCRIPT_MAX_RETRIES=2      # per-video retries when blocked (proxy only)
92	YT_TRANSCRIPT_BACKOFF=5          # seconds before the first retry
93	YT_BLOCKED_ABORT_THRESHOLD=3     # consecutive blocks before aborting the run
94	```
95	
96	Without a proxy the fetcher does **not** retry: the same blocked IP would fail
97	every attempt, so retrying only slows the run down before it aborts.
98	
99	## Output Artifacts
100	
101	| Path | Contents |
102	|------|----------|
103	| `data/playlist_ingestion/state.json` | Resume checkpoint (all episodes ever seen) |
104	| `data/playlist_ingestion/transcripts/<id>.txt` | Cleaned transcript (title + URL header) |
105	| `data/playlist_ingestion/reports/<id>.fidelity.json` | Full FidelityReport with subscores + issues |
106	| `data/playlist_ingestion/reports/run-<ts>.md` | Per-run markdown summary table |
107	
108	## Duplicate Fetch Note
109	
110	The fidelity stage fetches the transcript once for scoring, then
111	`main.process_url()` re-fetches it internally during ingestion. This is
112	deliberate: it keeps `main.py` untouched and the gate fully decoupled. The
113	transcript API is fast and the `--delay` flag (default 2s) keeps request
114	pacing polite. If YouTube rate-limits a long run, raise `--delay`.
115	
116	## Reviewing Quarantined Episodes
117	
118	```bash
119	# List quarantined episodes with their issues
120	python -c "
121	import json
122	s = json.load(open('data/playlist_ingestion/state.json'))
123	for vid, e in s['videos'].items():
124	    if e.get('status') == 'quarantined':
125	        print(f\"{vid}  {e.get('fidelity')}  {e['title'][:60]}\")
126	        for i in e.get('issues', []): print(f'   - {i}')
127	"
128	```
129	
130	To ingest one anyway after manual review, run the standard single-URL path:
131	
132	```bash
133	python main.py "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=<id>" --upload
134	```
135	
136	then update its state entry (or just leave it — `--force` is per-run, and the
137	single-URL path doesn't consult the playlist state file).
138	
139	## Tuning
140	
141	- `--min-fidelity 0.6` — stricter gate for noisy auto-captioned channels
142	- `--llm-review` — worth it for channels with heavy crosstalk; costs one
143	  chat completion per episode (`FIDELITY_REVIEW_MODEL`, default `gpt-5.5`)
144	- `--limit 5 --dry-run` — cheap preview of a new playlist's caption quality
145	  before committing to a full ingest
146	- Fidelity weights/thresholds live at the top of `lib/transcript_fidelity.py`
147
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	"""
2	Transcript Fidelity Review
3	
4	Scores a YouTube transcript's quality before it is ingested into the
5	knowledge base. Combines cheap deterministic heuristics (coverage, speech
6	density, gaps, caption artifacts, repetition) with an optional LLM coherence
7	review. Used by scripts/playlist_ingestion.py as a quality gate.
8	
9	All functions are fault-tolerant: a scoring failure returns a neutral result
10	rather than raising, matching the pipeline's never-block philosophy.
11	"""
12	
13	import json
14	import logging
15	import os
16	import re
17	from dataclasses import dataclass, field, asdict
18	from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional
19	
20	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
21	
22	# Bracketed caption cues that carry no speech content
23	CUE_PATTERN = re.compile(r"\[(?:music|applause|laughter|inaudible|foreign|__+|\s*)\]", re.IGNORECASE)
24	# Normal conversational speech falls in this words-per-minute band
25	WPM_LOW, WPM_HIGH = 90, 220
26	
27	
28	@dataclass
29	class FidelityReport:
30	    video_id: str
31	    score: float = 0.0                      # composite 0-1
32	    verdict: str = "unknown"                # pass | review | fail
33	    word_count: int = 0
34	    covered_seconds: float = 0.0
35	    expected_seconds: Optional[float] = None
36	    words_per_minute: Optional[float] = None
37	    max_gap_seconds: float = 0.0
38	    artifact_ratio: float = 0.0
39	    repetition_ratio: float = 0.0
40	    subscores: Dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)
41	    issues: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
42	    llm_review: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
43	
44	    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
45	        return asdict(self)
46	
47	
48	def clean_transcript(text: str) -> str:
49	    """Normalize a raw caption transcript into readable prose.
50	
51	    Strips non-speech cues, collapses whitespace, and de-duplicates
52	    consecutive identical lines (a common auto-caption artifact).
53	    """
54	    if not text:
55	        return ""
56	    text = CUE_PATTERN.sub(" ", text)
57	    lines = [ln.strip() for ln in text.splitlines()]
58	    deduped: List[str] = []
59	    for ln in lines:
60	        if not ln:
61	            continue
62	        if deduped and ln == deduped[-1]:
63	            continue
64	        deduped.append(ln)
65	    text = " ".join(deduped)
66	    return re.sub(r"\s{2,}", " ", text).strip()
67	
68	
69	def _seg_field(seg: Any, name: str, default: float = 0.0) -> float:
70	    """Read a timing field from a transcript segment.
71	
72	    youtube-transcript-api >= 1.0 yields FetchedTranscriptSnippet objects with
73	    attributes; older versions (and our cached fixtures) yield plain dicts.
74	    Support both — an AttributeError here silently zeroed every coverage metric
75	    and left the fidelity gate passing everything on its fallback score.
76	    """
77	    value = seg.get(name, default) if hasattr(seg, "get") else getattr(seg, name, default)
78	    try:
79	        return float(value)
80	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
81	        raise ValueError(f"non-numeric {name}: {value!r}")
82	
83	
84	def _segment_stats(segments: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Dict[str, float]:
85	    """Coverage and gap metrics from timed transcript segments."""
86	    covered_end = 0.0
87	    max_gap = 0.0
88	    prev_end = 0.0
89	    for seg in segments:
90	        try:
91	            start = _seg_field(seg, "start")
92	            duration = _seg_field(seg, "duration")
93	        except (TypeError, ValueError):
94	            continue
95	        if prev_end and start - prev_end > max_gap:
96	            max_gap = start - prev_end
97	        prev_end = max(prev_end, start + duration)
98	        covered_end = max(covered_end, start + duration)
99	    return {"covered_seconds": covered_end, "max_gap_seconds": max_gap}
100	
101	
102	def _repetition_ratio(text: str, window: int = 6) -> float:
103	    """Fraction of duplicated n-gram windows — high values mean stuck captions."""
104	    words = text.lower().split()
105	    if len(words) < window * 2:
106	        return 0.0
107	    grams = [" ".join(words[i:i + window]) for i in range(0, len(words) - window, window)]
108	    if not grams:
109	        return 0.0
110	    return 1.0 - (len(set(grams)) / len(grams))
111	
112	
113	def _taper(value: float, low: float, high: float, hard_low: float, hard_high: float) -> float:
114	    """1.0 inside [low, high], linear falloff to 0 at hard bounds."""
115	    if low <= value <= high:
116	        return 1.0
117	    if value < low:
118	        if value <= hard_low:
119	            return 0.0
120	        return (value - hard_low) / (low - hard_low)
121	    if value >= hard_high:
122	        return 0.0
123	    return (hard_high - value) / (hard_high - high)
124	
125	
126	def llm_coherence_review(text: str, video_id: str, model: Optional[str] = None,
127	                         samples: int = 3, sample_chars: int = 1500) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
128	    """Optional LLM pass: rate coherence of sampled transcript chunks 0-1.
129	
130	    Routed through the shared fallback chain (`lib.llm_fallback`), not a direct
131	    client. Until 2026-08-07 this constructed its own `OpenAI()` and defaulted
132	    to `gpt-5.5`, which meant fidelity review kept billing OpenAI directly
133	    after the enrichment chain had been moved off it, and inherited none of the
134	    chain's retry, dead-tier caching, or provider attribution.
135	
136	    `model` is now an optional *tier hint* (matched against tier ids), not a
137	    raw model name. Returns None on any failure — fidelity scoring degrades to
138	    its deterministic heuristics rather than blocking ingestion.
139	    """
140	    try:
141	        from lib.llm_fallback import LLMFallback
142	
143	        step = max(1, (len(text) - sample_chars) // max(1, samples - 1)) if len(text) > sample_chars else len(text)
144	        chunks = [text[i:i + sample_chars] for i in range(0, len(text), step)][:samples]
145	
146	        system_prompt = (
147	            "You are reviewing machine-generated podcast transcript excerpts for fidelity. "
148	            "Rate overall coherence from 0.0 (garbled, unusable) to 1.0 (clean, fully readable), "
149	            "and list concrete issues (garbled phrases, mid-sentence truncation, wrong-language text, "
150	            "caption artifacts). Respond ONLY with JSON: "
151	            '{"coherence": <float>, "issues": [<strings>]}'
152	        )
153	        hint = model or os.getenv("FIDELITY_REVIEW_PROVIDER") or None
154	        result = LLMFallback(prefer_provider=hint).complete(
155	            system_prompt=system_prompt,
156	            user_content="\n---\n".join(chunks),
157	        )
158	
159	        raw = re.sub(r"^```(?:json)?|```$", "", result.text.strip(), flags=re.MULTILINE).strip()
160	        data = json.loads(raw)
161	        return {
162	            # Record the tier that actually served it, not the one requested —
163	            # attribution has to survive a silent fallback.
164	            "model": result.tier_id,
165	            "provider": result.provider,
166	            "degraded": result.degraded,
167	            "coherence": max(0.0, min(1.0, float(data.get("coherence", 0.5)))),
168	            "issues": [str(i) for i in data.get("issues", [])][:10],
169	        }
170	    except Exception as e:
171	        logger.warning(f"LLM coherence review skipped for {video_id}: {e}")
172	        return None
173	
174	
175	def review_transcript(
176	    transcript: str,
177	    video_id: str,
178	    segments: Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] = None,
179	    expected_duration_seconds: Optional[float] = None,
180	    use_llm: bool = False,
181	    llm_model: Optional[str] = None,
182	) -> FidelityReport:
183	    """Score transcript fidelity 0-1 and assign a verdict.
184	
185	    Verdicts: 'pass' (>= 0.7), 'review' (0.45-0.7), 'fail' (< 0.45).
186	    """
187	    report = FidelityReport(video_id=video_id)
188	    try:
189	        raw = transcript or ""
190	        cleaned = clean_transcript(raw)
191	        words = cleaned.split()
192	        report.word_count = len(words)
193	
194	        if report.word_count < 50:
195	            report.verdict = "fail"
196	            report.issues.append(f"Transcript too short ({report.word_count} words)")
197	            return report
198	
199	        # Artifact ratio measured against the raw text before cleaning
200	        cues = len(CUE_PATTERN.findall(raw))
201	        raw_tokens = max(1, len(raw.split()))
202	        report.artifact_ratio = round(cues / raw_tokens, 4)
203	
204	        report.repetition_ratio = round(_repetition_ratio(cleaned), 4)
205	
206	        seg_stats = _segment_stats(segments or [])
207	        report.covered_seconds = round(seg_stats["covered_seconds"], 1)
208	        report.max_gap_seconds = round(seg_stats["max_gap_seconds"], 1)
209	        report.expected_seconds = expected_duration_seconds
210	
211	        # --- subscores ---
212	        subs: Dict[str, float] = {}
213	
214	        if expected_duration_seconds and report.covered_seconds:
215	            coverage = min(1.0, report.covered_seconds / expected_duration_seconds)
216	            subs["coverage"] = coverage
217	            if coverage < 0.8:
218	                report.issues.append(
219	                    f"Captions cover only {coverage:.0%} of the {expected_duration_seconds:.0f}s episode")
220	        else:
221	            subs["coverage"] = 0.75  # unknown duration: mild neutral prior
222	
223	        minutes = (report.covered_seconds or (expected_duration_seconds or 0)) / 60.0
224	        if minutes > 0.5:
225	            wpm = report.word_count / minutes
226	            report.words_per_minute = round(wpm, 1)
227	            subs["density"] = _taper(wpm, WPM_LOW, WPM_HIGH, 30, 400)
228	            if subs["density"] < 0.5:
229	                report.issues.append(f"Abnormal speech density ({wpm:.0f} wpm)")
230	        else:
231	            subs["density"] = 0.75
232	
233	        subs["gaps"] = _taper(report.max_gap_seconds, 0, 20, 0, 180)
234	        if report.max_gap_seconds > 60:
235	            report.issues.append(f"Caption gap of {report.max_gap_seconds:.0f}s detected")
236	
237	        subs["artifacts"] = max(0.0, 1.0 - report.artifact_ratio * 5)
238	        if report.artifact_ratio > 0.05:
239	            report.issues.append(f"High non-speech cue ratio ({report.artifact_ratio:.1%})")
240	
241	        subs["repetition"] = max(0.0, 1.0 - report.repetition_ratio * 4)
242	        if report.repetition_ratio > 0.15:
243	            report.issues.append(f"Repeated caption blocks ({report.repetition_ratio:.1%} duplicate n-grams)")
244	
245	        weights = {"coverage": 0.30, "density": 0.20, "gaps": 0.15, "artifacts": 0.15, "repetition": 0.20}
246	        score = sum(subs[k] * w for k, w in weights.items())
247	
248	        if use_llm:
249	            report.llm_review = llm_coherence_review(cleaned, video_id, model=llm_model)
250	            if report.llm_review:
251	                # LLM verdict counts for a third of the final score when available
252	                score = score * (2 / 3) + report.llm_review["coherence"] * (1 / 3)
253	                report.issues.extend(report.llm_review.get("issues", []))
254	
255	        report.subscores = {k: round(v, 3) for k, v in subs.items()}
256	        report.score = round(score, 3)
257	        report.verdict = "pass" if score >= 0.7 else ("review" if score >= 0.45 else "fail")
258	        return report
259	    except Exception as e:
260	        logger.warning(f"Fidelity review failed for {video_id}: {e}")

_**User (2026-08-08 02:23:27Z)**_

Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Calibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page — what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

When unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first — CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world — its materials, instruments, vernacular — is where distinctive choices come from. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.

**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. The Artifact CSP blocks font CDNs, so don't link a webfont URL and risk a silent fallback. Instead inline the face as a @font-face data URI. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.

**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject — the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.

**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme: `prefers-color-scheme` carries the OS preference, and the viewer's toggle stamps `data-theme="dark"` / `data-theme="light"` on the root element, which must override the media query in both directions. The robust pattern is token-level: define the palette as custom properties on `:root`, redefine only the tokens under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` — style components through the tokens, never directly inside the media query — then redefine them again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]` and `:root[data-theme="light"]`. Give the second theme the same care as the first — don't naively invert; keep contrast legible and the accent working on both grounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme — make it a choice, not an omission.

**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content — tables, code, diagrams — gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks; visual bugs hide in the gap between source and output. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.

**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out — a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.

**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen — name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it — no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.

**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number — a pill, a chip, a severity stripe — so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.



## Process

Before writing code, sketch a short design plan — a compact token system with color, type, and layout:
- **Color**: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles — a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.

Then build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.

## When the request is editorial

The stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world — headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. 
- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. 
- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.

# Appendix — Microfilm Dark canvas chrome (historical sketch)

Codified 2026-07-08 from `apps/app/src/components/design-system/{ARCHIVAL_DYSTOPIAN_AESTHETIC,RESEARCH_CANVAS_AESTHETIC,DESIGN_SYSTEM}.md` plus the live canvas chrome. Register: **partial product chrome**, not full design.

## Scene

A researcher at 23:00 in a dim room, arranging declassified records on a large monitor. The canvas is the reading table; panels are documents pulled into the lamplight. Dark is forced by the scene: the luminous graph is the subject, chrome recedes into the desk.

## Concept

**Microfilm Dark**: the archival dossier aesthetic (manila, typewriter, stamps, redaction) photographed at night. Not neon cyberpunk; HUD elements are digital ghosts at low opacity. Institutional, clinical, slightly ominous.

This is **one lighting condition / register moment** for the Research Canvas — not the whole Ultraterrestrial design ambition (see `DESIGN_REGISTERS.md`).

## Color (OKLCH, warm-tinted toward manila hue ≈85)

Strategy: Restrained neutrals + a semantic evidentiary palette (data-viz exception).

| Token | Value | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `--ut-void` | `oklch(0.16 0.006 85)` | canvas base |
| `--ut-surface` | `oklch(0.21 0.008 85 / 0.88)` | panel base (dark manila glass) |
| `--ut-surface-2` | `oklch(0.25 0.01 85 / 0.9)` | raised layer (tooltips, chips) |

| `--ut-paper` | `oklch(0.93 0.015 90)` | primary text (never #fff) |
| `--ut-ink-dim` | `oklch(0.93 0.015 90 / 0.62)` | secondary text |

| `--ut-stamp` | `oklch(0.58 0.19 27)` | stamped red — classification, Disconfirmed |

Semantic evidentiary hues (existing, kept): emerald = documented/observed, violet = AI/resonant, amber = temporal/contested, zinc = unverified, red = disconfirmed.

**Provenance delineation rule**: solid borders = sourced/deterministic content; **dashed borders = AI inference** (the analytical layer, per the terminology ruling). Never mix.

For the live scorer, I'm implementing threshold logic where verdicts fail if the score drops below the minimum fidelity or if explicitly marked as failed, with quarantine tracking. The scoring system cleans the transcript by stripping cue patterns like music and applause markers, calculates word count from the cleaned text, computes artifact ratio from cue density, detects repetition patterns across sliding windows, and derives subscores for coverage and density metrics.

I'm realizing that with zero duration input, the live scorer defaults coverage to 0.75 and density becomes weak since both covered and expected segments are zero—only artifacts and repetition vary meaningfully. To make this more robust, I should let users optionally provide episode duration in seconds, which would let coverage and density actually compute based on real segment data rather than defaults. The duration would serve as the expected duration, while covered duration comes from the actual segments detected.
